title: Global small-strain J2 plasticity
summary: Three-dimensional and two-dimensional axisymmetric Mises plasticity with linear isotropic hardening, a shared quadrature transaction, analytical algorithmic tangent, cyclic amplitude paths, physical-increment cutback, portable restart, standard fields, and work/energy histories verified on homogeneous, nonuniform, and public thick-cylinder paths.

science.statement: An elastic trial stress is projected radially onto a linearly hardened Mises surface; the same return map supplies stress, history and its analytical consistent derivative to global Newton equilibrium.

equations.label: yield function
equations.description: A nonpositive trial value remains elastic.

equations.label: plastic multiplier
equations.description: Closed-form increment for associative J2 flow with linear isotropic hardening.

equations.label: global equilibrium
equations.description: Newton iterations use trial state based on the last committed increment.

inputs.name: total strain
inputs.type: symmetric 3x3 tensor at every quadrature point
inputs.description: Small total strain at the current global iterate.

inputs.name: material parameters
inputs.type: E, nu, initial yield stress, hardening modulus

outputs.name: S
outputs.description: Accepted Cauchy stress retained at the constitutive integration points after convergence.

outputs.name: MISES
outputs.description: Pointwise invariant of S; the visualization helper writes a separately identifiable DG0 cell average.

outputs.name: PE and PEEQ
outputs.description: Plastic strain tensor and equivalent plastic strain.

outputs.name: RF and internal-energy diagnostics
outputs.type: nodal residual field and scalar result quantities
outputs.description: Full nodal residual plus elastic, hardening, plastic-dissipation, internal-energy, prescribed-work, and balance histories.

assumptions: Small strain, either three spatial dimensions or a two-dimensional axisymmetric meridian.
Rate independence, associative Mises flow, and linear isotropic hardening.
Natural loads and nonzero engineering Dirichlet targets share one named amplitude; the step coordinate remains monotone while amplitude values may reverse.
conventions: Committed history is immutable during a rejected Newton iterate.
Tensor storage is full symmetric 3x3 form rather than engineering Voigt.
The normalized step coordinate runs from zero to one; load amplitude may be non-monotone.
maximum_inelastic_increment limits the equivalent plastic-strain increment and triggers rollback/cutback after an otherwise converged Newton attempt.
applicability: Monotone or reviewed tabular cyclic small-strain 3D or axisymmetric solid loading within the implemented isotropic-hardening law.
Laboratory-scale regression and research workflows requiring inspectable state.
Nonuniform displacement-controlled structures with simultaneous elastic and plastic integration points.
limitations: There is no plane-stress local constraint, finite-strain plasticity, or kinematic hardening.
External-work histories are currently available for nonzero strong prescribed displacements; natural, weak, and affine-MPC work require separate verified definitions.
The public thick-cylinder route verifies first yield; cyclic hardening still requires an external structure-level benchmark.

usage.minimal_example: Register J2LinearIsotropicHardening in a 3D nonlinear_static Model, add supports and traction, then call model.step(target=u, material=steel, incrementation=steps.automatic()).

validation_rules: Reject unsupported dimensional assumptions and nonphysical material parameters.
Commit shared transaction state only after global and constitutive-increment acceptance.
Restore field, constitutive state, adaptive next-increment state, energy history, accepted/attempt histories, and execution events after restart.
